name: Aqara Hub M2 (EU)

radios.note: Zigbee 3.0, Bluetooth LE 5.0, 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi, one RJ-45 Ethernet port and an IR transmitter. No model number on the page.

matter.note: The product page does not mention Matter; no CSA listing found.

apple_home.note: Through HomeKit. Aqara Zigbee devices appear in Apple Home; the IR controller is not exposed there.

google_home.note: Aqara lists Apple HomeKit, Google Assistant, Alexa and IFTTT. For IR devices, only some types such as TVs and air conditioners work with Google Assistant and Alexa.

alexa.note: Aqara lists Apple HomeKit, Google Assistant, Alexa and IFTTT. For IR devices, only some types such as TVs and air conditioners work with Google Assistant and Alexa.

smartthings.note: Not mentioned on the maker pages.

home_assistant.note: Not confirmed by an official source.

localControl.note: Aqara says local automations keep running if the internet goes down.

deviceProtocols.note: Works only with Aqara Zigbee child devices, not other brands or Aqara Thread devices. Built-in IR controller for TVs, fans and air conditioners. It has a BLE 5.0 radio, but the page does not say it pairs Bluetooth devices.

matterBridge.note: The M2 pages do not mention Matter; Aqara's US M2 page points to the Hub M3 for Matter.

threadBorderRouter.note: Aqara says it does not support Aqara Thread devices and lists no Thread radio, but no page states whether it is a border router.

maxDevices.note: Aqara Zigbee child devices; repeaters such as a plug or wall switch are required.

summary: Aqara Hub M2 (EU) links Aqara Zigbee 3.0 devices to Apple Home, Google Home and Alexa, with Wi-Fi, an Ethernet port and a built-in IR controller. Aqara says it handles up to 128 child devices, and local automations keep running if the internet drops. The pages don't mention Matter, and SmartThings and Home Assistant are unconfirmed.
caveats: It pairs only with Aqara Zigbee devices, not other brands.
Google Home and Alexa control only some IR device types, such as TVs and air conditioners.
The IR controller is not exposed to Apple Home.
Aqara says repeater devices such as a smart plug are needed to reach 128 devices.
